thread_text:
mina: Hi team — my sabbatical week overlaps the company year-end shutdown and also falls on a religious observance. Do I get to carry my floating holiday into next year or get an exception?

arun: Curious too  we can get an exception path here. Mina the shutdown dates were published after I booked mine as well.

sam (People Ops): Quick TL;DR: floating holidays expire at year-end by default. If the observance prevented you from taking the day earlier and you can provide a verification (calendar invite, community org note, or brief statement), we can evaluate an exception.

sam (People Ops): Process: 1) Submit a Time Off request for the observance date marked as "Floating Holiday" or "PTO" with note "Religious observance - year-end shutdown conflict". 2) Email people-ops@redwood with subject "Year-end observance exception" and attach verification. 3) Manager confirms in reply. People Ops will review and either approve carryover to next calendar year or authorize admin pay/comp depending on circumstances.

mina: What counts as verification? I can attach the event invite from my community center and a short note.

sam (People Ops): That should be sufficient. If it's an ongoing recurring observance, a short statement is fine. For one-off requests we prefer an event invite or link. We prioritize minimal friction.

arun: If approved for carryover, is there a hard cap on how many floating days can be carried?

sam (People Ops): Yes  we approve carryover it's limited to one floating holiday per employee and must be used within Q1 of the following year. We document the approval in the HR portal.

people-ops-bot: Reminder: Deadline to submit exception requests for year-end shutdown is Dec 29 23:59 PT.

mina: Thanks, submitting now. Manager copied.

payroll-bot: Note for managers: if admin pay is requested instead of carryover, email payroll@redwood with employee ID and code ADMINPAY. Processing takes up to 3 business days.

mina: Appreciate the quick clarification!
